step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts a high-scale travel platform (Al Musafir / Seera Group) handling approximately 300k requests/minute. Content and initial requests originate from users (UserConsumerWebMobile) and enter CloudFront. Static assets are fetched from S3 into CloudFront, while Lambda@Edge performs intelligent edge routing based on device type and region. CloudFront routes incoming traffic to a group of around 60 Load Balancers (ELB), which split traffic between legacy monolithic systems on EC2 and containerized microservices on EKS (~250 microservices across 1400 pods). On the data layer, both legacy and EKS services interact with self-managed MongoDB and Kafka running on EC2 instances, while EKS microservices also connect to RDS for transactional database operations. Monitoring infrastructure includes self-managed tools on EC2 (Prometheus, ELK) alongside CloudWatch for pod health, logging, and alerts.

graph.name: Seera Group Microservices Architecture
graph.notes: Architectural transcription of Seera Group's migration from legacy monolithic EC2 workloads to microservices hosted on AWS EKS with edge routing via CloudFront/Lambda@Edge.

edges.notes: User traffic routes into CloudFront CDN.
Static content served from S3 through CloudFront.
Lambda@Edge provides routing intelligence based on client region/device.
